newsitem.title: USA: Illinois River area still closed - US Coast Guard.
newsitem.headline: Illinois River area still closed - US Coast Guard.

text.p: One stretch of the Illinois River remained closed to navigation on Monday as a result of high water fed by recent rainfall, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

River mile 120 at Havana, Ill., to mile 187.3 at Lacon, Ill., was closed on Monday. Elsewhere, from mile 120 to mile zero at Grafton, Ill, speed restrictions to navigation were imposed on March 2, said Drew Cheney, assistant chief of port operations, Coast Guard, Marine Safety Office..
"Traffic below Havana, Ill., at mile 120 may transit north and southbound at the slowest and safest speed with no more than 12 barges," Cheney said.
Peoria Lock, located in the closed river zone was shut down, said Mike Zerbonia, chief maintenance section, Illinois Waterway Project, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
He noted from mile 187.3 at Lacon to Chicago, no restrictions were imposed. But on Friday, the Coast Guard allowed some stranded river traffic through the closed areas.
"Normally that is what we do. We don't like to keep vessels stranded in a closed area. In some situations, there are tows that may be stranded but we allow some light boats to move," Cheney said.
Zerbonia said the river has not receded in some areas.

The Illinois River at Peoria will crest on March 4 at 27 feet. "It is currently at 26.9 feet and flood stage is at 18 feet," Zerbonia said. "At Beardstown, Ill., the crest was predicted on March 5 at 24.5 feet compared to 23.5 feet at 0800 CST, Monday. Flood stage is at 14 feet."
Also, Zerbonia said Starved Rock Lock near Utica, opened on Saturday and remained open but with loading restrictions.
The Corps continued to issue sandbags to municipalities and levee districts as needed.
"The municipalities of Rome and Liverpool were still flooded and the river has not receded in either area so far," Zerbonia said.
But Zerbonia said forecast for of dry weather this week for central Illinois should allow the river to recede.
"The Illinois River has begun to fall in Morris, Ill., at mile 263, on Sunday all the way down to Henry, Ill. at mile 196.1," Zerbonia said.
The Coast Guard has also established a safety zone on the upper Mississippi River due to high water from river mile 184 to 179.

"What that means is that all tows must have a minimum of 250 horsepower per 1500 tons per cargo," the Coast Guard's Cheney said. "Southbound tows more than 600 feet in length excluding tow boats may transit the safety zone during daylight hours only."
Cheney said the safety zone will remain in effect until the St Louis river gauge indicates less than 25 feet.
Early Monday, the St Louis river gauge was 31.3 feet, Cheney said.
